canonicalExplanation.summary: `if / else if / else` checks conditions in order and runs the first true branch; `switch` compares one value against cases with `===` (remember `break`!). Conditions use **truthiness**, so `if (count)` treats a real 0 as "missing" and `if (items)` treats an empty array `[]` as present. For boundary-complete logic, check exactly what you mean: `count == null` (null or undefined), `items.length === 0`, and test every threshold.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A notifications badge should show "–" when the count hasn't loaded yet, and "0" when there are truly no messages. `if (count) show(count) else show("–")` shows "–" for zero — wrong! A nullish check distinguishes a missing count from a legitimate zero. In this lesson you'll implement and test boundary-complete conditional logic.

examples.title: Missing count vs zero
examples.situation: A nullish check distinguishes missing count from a legitimate zero.
walkthrough: **Bug:** `if (count)` treats 0 as falsy, so a real zero shows "–".
**Nullish check:** `if (count == null) return "–"` only matches null and undefined — the missing count.
**Test:** badgeText(undefined) → "–", badgeText(0) → "0", badgeText(99) → "99", badgeText(100) will return "99+".
examples.result: The badge shows "–" while loading and "0" for a legitimate zero, with every boundary tested.

examples.title: The switch that fell through
examples.situation: `switch (role) { case "editor": canEdit = true; case "admin": canDelete = true; }` — editors can suddenly delete posts.
walkthrough: There is no `break` after the editor case, so execution falls through into the admin case.
Editors therefore get canEdit and canDelete.
Fix: add `break` to every case, and make intentional fall-through explicit with a comment or separate checks.
examples.result: Each role gets exactly its permissions, whatever the case order.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: An empty array is falsy because it contains no elements.
misconceptions.correction: All objects, including empty arrays and objects, are truthy. Test contents explicitly with length (or Object.keys for objects), and test missing values with == null.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, why did the empty array log "has items"?

analogy.example: Truthiness checks are like **asking "is there a box?" instead of "is there anything in the box?"** An empty box still counts as a box. Ask the question you actually mean.
usefulFor: explicit checks for missing, empty, zero
limitations: Boxes can't be null; JavaScript values can.
switch is like a sorting office that keeps sliding parcels down unless each chute has a stop (break).

remediation.explanation: For each condition, write the **values that should pass and fail**, including undefined, null, 0, "", [] and each threshold ±1. If any surprises you, replace the truthiness check with an explicit one.

recap.summary: To implement boundary-complete conditional logic, say exactly what you check — == null for missing, === 0 for zero, length === 0 for empty — put breaks in every switch case, and test missing, zero and both sides of each threshold.
